test_title: PYST 6: SSC GD Constable 2024 - English (Held On: 21 Feb, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I want to __loose weight,__ yet I eat chocolate daily.
solution:
The correct answer is: **lose weight**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word 'loose' is incorrect in this context as it means *not tight or free from constraints*.
 
• The appropriate word in the context is 'lose', which means *to have less of something, especially weight*.
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be 'lose weight' instead of 'loose weight.'

Correct sentence: *I want to lose weight, yet I eat chocolate daily*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Loose vs. Lose:

 
 
• Loose: *not firmly or tightly fixed in place*.

 
 
• ***Example:** The shirt is loose*.
 
 
 
• Lose: *become unable to find* or *fail to keep*.
 
 
• ***Example:** I want to lose weight*.
 
 
 
 
 
• Common mistake: Many people confuse 'loose' with 'lose' due to the similarity in spelling and pronunciation.
